title: Climbing the Ladder with Ronnie
description: Career advice hour on Snazzie FM. Ronnie reads listeners' workplace letters with total warmth, then gives advice that would get anyone escorted from the building. Barry has read the HR handbook. It does not help.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and it's time to get ahead. This is Climbing the Ladder, the hour where your dead-end job meets its match. <p:0.3> Me.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I do want to say up top, I read the H R handbook this week. Cover to cover.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And we're all very proud of you, Barry. Now let's open the mailbag.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: First one. Denise from accounts payable writes, quote, I've done the same job for nine years. I've trained three people who all got promoted over me. My boss keeps saying the timing's never right for a raise. <p:0.3> I just want to ask for what I'm worth without sounding pushy.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Oh, that's a good one. That's a fair, human ask.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It is, Barry, so here's what you don't do. You don't ASK. Asking is for people who get told no. <p:0.3> Denise, the move is simple. Tomorrow morning, you put the title you want on your email signature, and you let H R catch up to reality.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, you... you can't promote yourself. That's not how titles work.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That right there is the exact thinking that's kept her at the same desk for nine years. <p:0.3> And Denise, to make it official? C C the whole company.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The whole company.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Every single one. Now they all know your name AND your title. You're welcome, Denise.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Next letter. Marcus, who didn't give his last name, writes, quote, a coworker took credit for my project in a big meeting. The manager believed him. Now HE'S up for the lead role on the thing I actually built. <p:0.3> I want to set the record straight without looking petty or starting a war.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's painful. Marcus just wants the truth out there.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, Marcus, you're framing this as a problem. It's a branding opportunity. <p:0.3> Here's the play. You take credit for his NEXT project. Right now. Preemptively. Evens the whole ledger.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's just... that's doing the bad thing back at him.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Yes! Exactly, Barry, now you're getting it! And to lock it in, Marcus, you C C the whole company so everybody knows the project was, quote, always yours.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It wasn't, though. It was the coworker's next project. We literally just said that.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Was it, Barry? <p:0.3> Or was it always Marcus's? C C the company. Let the inbox decide.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Okay, Barry, you read this next one. I'm parched.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Sure. Priya from the night shift writes, quote, my new manager schedules urgent calls at eleven at night, texts me on weekends, and calls me not a team player if I don't reply within minutes. <p:0.3> I'm exhausted. I want to set a boundary without getting labeled difficult.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: And Ronnie, I think the answer here is pretty clear. She needs to log off.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Log off? Priya, congratulations, you have an ENGAGED boss. <p:0.3> This isn't a boundary problem. This is a visibility opportunity. You out-text him.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Out-text him?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Reply at three in the morning. Then four. You escalate the availability until SHE is the dedicated one in this relationship. He texts Saturday? She texts Sunday. At dawn.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's, that is textbook how people burn out.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Burnout, Barry, is just ambition that hasn't been promoted yet. <p:0.3> And Priya? Loop in the whole company on those late-night replies. C C every last one of them. Let them all SEE the hours.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: There it is again. The whole company.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It works every time, Barry. Last letter of the night, and this one's a doozy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Walter, sixty-one, writes, quote, my whole department is being quietly restructured, and I'm pretty sure my role is on the chopping block. I've got two years till retirement. <p:0.3> I just want to know how to protect my position, or land softly.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay. Walter is two years from the finish line. This one we keep gentle, Ronnie. Please.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Gentle? Walter, you get AHEAD of it. You announce your OWN promotion. To a role that does not currently exist. <p:0.3> Director of Restructuring.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Director of... no. No, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And then, Walter, you restructure the people who are restructuring you. You get to them first.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, do not tell him to C C the company on this one. I am begging you.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Walter. C C the whole company. The board. The building. <p:0.3> And whoever does the parking.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Hhh. <p:0.3> Okay.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: [question-en] Barry? You've gone quiet on me.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I'm fine. I'm just resting my eyes. And my career.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Before we go, an update. Walter wrote back. <p:0.3> The Director of Restructuring email reached four hundred people, the actual board, and a vendor in another country.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Beautiful reach. Go on.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Walter has been escorted out of the building. But, quote, two of the people who were laying me off got laid off in the confusion, so I'm calling that a draw.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He C C'd the whole company, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: <p:0.3> Atta boy, Walter.
